A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OPeRA dataset and ShoppingFlow benchmark. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable across all 18 pages of v3 and 19 pages of v5, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V3 reports original shopping-data analyses and experiments with four LLMs, including next-action prediction and joint rationale/action generation in Tables 4–5.

after.justification: V5 reports original dataset analyses, next-action prediction results, and model-error analyses in Tables 5–8, including appendix results.

M1.justification: The published prediction prompt changes: v3 Appendix H includes a standalone purchase output and click_type/selector fields; v5 Appendix I removes them and specifies clicks by name. This revises the documented inference interface. The collection/parsing pipeline and zero-shot LLM approach remain unchanged.

E1.justification: V3 evaluates next-action prediction and a separate joint rationale/action generation task with 48 instances. V5 removes the latter task and its evaluation, including from the appendices. The Amazon dataset and participant coverage remain unchanged; the new outcome metrics examine terminal actions within the retained shopping sessions.

E2.justification: The corresponding next-action comparisons retain GPT-4.1, Claude-3.7-Sonnet, DeepSeek-R1, and Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct, with the same persona/history-rationale ablation variants. Newly cited methods such as Shop-R1 are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Click exact matching changes from requiring subtype and target agreement to target-name agreement. V5 separately reports weighted and macro action-type F1 and adds click-subtype and session-outcome metrics. BERTScore/ROUGE-L evaluation disappears with joint generation. The stated zero-shot setup and 15-user, 90-session selection remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V5 adds systematic error decomposition in Table 6, distinguishing missed action types, incorrect buttons, and input-field/text errors. Table 7 newly compares predicted and observed action frequencies, exposing underprediction of termination. Next-action input ablations and Appendix F's segmentation analysis are retained; joint-generation ablations disappear with that task.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new error percentages and F1 scores are frequencies and point estimates, not uncertainty reporting. Appendix F's percentile-based segmentation justification is unchanged.

E6.justification: Unablated action accuracies are replaced: GPT-4.1 18.53% to 21.51%, Claude 7.54% to 10.75%, DeepSeek-R1 6.98% to 14.75%, and Llama 5.40% to 8.31%. DeepSeek now ranks above Claude on this metric. Changed prompts/scoring prevent interpreting these as same-setting gains. Joint-generation results are removed, while click/outcome scores and error distributions are added.

T1.justification: V5 removes the formal joint-task mapping from interaction history and persona to the action/rationale pair in v3 Section 4.1.2. Dataset notation and the next-action function remain unchanged. Neither version contains theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same contributions: a public dataset combining observations, personas, rationales, and actions, and a benchmark supporting personalized behavior simulation. They still describe rationale prediction despite removal of its experiment. Mentioning OPeRA-test earlier in v5 does not change the previously documented benchmark scope.

C2.justification: V3 emphasizes GPT's benefit from personas and improved action prediction through joint rationale generation. V5 drops the joint-generation interpretation and argues that personas mainly aid action semantics while potentially introducing noise into exact decisions. It newly interprets missed termination as possible task-completion bias and revises model-specific explanations. The reduced-action-space and omitted-visual-input limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix G adds operational descriptions of the 13 existing click categories. Prompt documentation is revised and the joint-generation prompt removed. V5 newly reports n=902 in result captions without explaining its relationship to the retained 992-action setup. Collection, parser, and segmentation details in Appendices A–F and the dataset-access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V5 adds seven citations, including Shop-R1, Customer-R1, See, Think, Act, and Trajectory2Task, and removes the BERTScore and ROUGE references. These are localized citation changes without substantial repositioning. Lu et al. (2025a) retains the same arXiv identifier under an updated title and is not a newly introduced work.

P1.justification: Rewriting and reorganization concentrate in Section 4: the joint-task subsection disappears, and Main Results and Error Analysis sections appear. Limitations are shortened, Appendix G expands, and prompts move from H to I. The abstract, conclusion, dataset narrative, and Appendices A–F remain largely or entirely unchanged.

P2.justification: The experimental displays are substantially reorganized: v3's single-column action and joint-result tables give way to an expanded full-width action table, two error-analysis tables, and a fuller appendix table. V3 Figure 4's click-distribution pie chart becomes v5 Table 3 with unchanged counts. Figures 1–3 retain their artwork, with Figure 3 relocated.

improvement.justification: V5 makes next-action evaluation more informative through separate F1 averages, click/outcome metrics, clearer category descriptions, and systematic error analysis. However, it removes v3's joint rationale/action experiment while retaining claims about evaluating rationale prediction, and leaves the 992-action setup versus 902-instance results unexplained. The stronger action diagnostics and loss of evidence for a retained central claim create material tradeoffs without a reliably assessable net quality direction.
